title: Siegard specification frontmatter
description: Frontmatter contract for a specification in specs/, the repository's first normative source. The body format and the section vocabulary are enforced by scripts/validate_specs.py; the status vocabulary is defined in docs/adr/README.md and shared with schemas/adr.v1.json and schemas/concept.v1.json. Supersession is structured here so a validator can decide it rather than a reader inferring it.

id.description: Four-digit sequential id, never reused, matching the filename prefix. Must be a quoted string: YAML reads an unquoted 0010 as octal 8 and an unquoted 0008 as a string, so the unquoted form is neither safe nor type-stable.

title.description: What the specification governs, stated as an outcome.

status.description: Lifecycle vocabulary defined in docs/adr/README.md. Only a maintainer, or a deterministic approval mechanism this repository defines, may change this value away from proposed. A proposed specification carries no normative weight and binds nothing.

contract_version.description: A consumer rejects an artifact it was not built to read rather than inferring version from shape.

superseded_by.description: Id of the specification that replaced this one. Required when status is superseded, and forbidden otherwise: a supersession relation that points nowhere, or points from a live specification, is a defect rather than history. The target must be a specification in specs/ — a specification is never superseded by an ADR, which sits below it in the precedence order.

Stating a replacement is what makes a specification superseded. Expressed as a dependency rather than as a negated allOf branch so the failure names the offending field instead of dumping the document.
